name: SFIA news: Volt Athletics acquires ZAMA Health for AI athlete development
title: SFIA news: Volt Athletics acquires ZAMA Health for AI athlete development
answer: This is a news item published by the Sports & Fitness Industry Association, the trade body that tracks participation and equipment-market research, reporting that Volt Athletics acquired ZAMA Health on April 9, 2024. The most useful detail for readers following AI in sports is that Volt's patented artificial intelligence adapts training to each individual, and the platform now serves nearly 2 million people while adding mental health and wellness tools.

sections.body: The Sports & Fitness Industry Association, a trade body known for participation and equipment-market research, published this news item on its website on April 9, 2024. It is a short announcement of a corporate acquisition rather than a research report or guidance document, and it sits within the association's resources section alongside other industry news. Its scope is limited to the two companies involved and the rationale for the deal.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Volt Athletics acquired ZAMA Health on April 9, 2024, adding mental health and wellness tools to its artificial intelligence powered athlete development platform. Volt was founded by Dan Giuliani and Trevor Watkins and first launched in 2013. It uses patented artificial intelligence and a performance training platform that dynamically adapts to each individual, delivering hyper-personalized training at scale. Volt has served nearly 2 million individuals worldwide, including collegiate and professional teams, first responders, military personnel and corporate entities. ZAMA is an athlete mental health and wellness platform built for collegiate athletes and staff, offering educational programming, self-guided modules, peer-to-peer support and custom integrations with on-campus resources. It partners directly with athletic departments to help them meet the NCAA's requirements around mental health best practices, and collaborates with clinics across the country to give departments direct access to therapy and psychiatry services when necessary. Brendan Sullivan, founder and chief executive of ZAMA Health, joins Volt as general manager of athlete wellbeing, and ZAMA's technology platform will initially operate as a distinct service within the Volt ecosystem.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that Volt Athletics was founded in 2013 and has served nearly 2 million individuals worldwide. It says Volt uses patented artificial intelligence and delivers hyper-personalized training at scale. It reports the acquisition date of April 9, 2024, and that ZAMA's platform will initially operate as a distinct service within the Volt ecosystem. It also notes ZAMA received early investments from Techstars and One Mind, and that its advisory board includes Jen Huberty, former head of science at Calm, and Gene DeFilippo, former athletic director at Boston College and Villanova.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in sports gets a concrete example of consolidation in athlete development technology, where an AI-driven training platform absorbs a mental health provider to broaden the services wrapped around the athlete. The item shows how personalization at scale is being positioned as the core value of AI in training, and how compliance with NCAA mental health requirements is becoming a commercial channel for such platforms. It also illustrates the investor and advisory networks forming around sports technology, including professional players and former athletic directors.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Sports

sections.body: This is a single news announcement, not research, data or guidance from the association itself. It gives no independent evaluation of the technology, no participation or market figures, and no detail on how the artificial intelligence works beyond the claim that it is patented and adaptive. The claims about scale and capability come from the companies involved, and the item is dated April 2024, so later developments are not covered.
